Summary: The command: Recite the firstfruits confession (Deuteronomy 26:5). Bringing the basket of firstfruits, Israel confessed: a Syrian ready to perish was my father, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt into this land.
Commandment: Recite the firstfruits confession, as prescribed in Deuteronomy 26:5.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The New Testament keeps the principle in a new key: Christ is the firstfruits of them that slept (1 Corinthians 15:20), and Christians are urged to give first and cheerfully, not by the old basket rite (2 Corinthians 9:7). The rite belongs to the land and the sanctuary; the first-giving heart it taught does not expire with it.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the confession itself gives the reason — 'a Syrian ready to perish was my father,' and God brought Israel out of Egypt and gave them this land (Deuteronomy 26:5-10).
